The test image shows a single corn plant completely wilted and dead — brown/tan dried leaves throughout, while surrounding plants are healthy green. This is a whole-plant systemic symptom, suggesting a stalk rot or wilt disease.

Top candidates: Goss's Wilt, Stewart's Disease, Bacterial Stalk Rot, Charcoal Stalk Rot, Diplodia Stalk Rot, Fusarium Disease.

Let me view reference images across 8 classes.
Bacterial Stalk Rot is a strong match — single dead plant, brown wilted leaves, healthy neighbors. Let me check a few more candidates.

The evidence is clear. The Bacterial_Stalk_Rot reference (Corn_Disease_42) is a near-identical match to the test image: single corn plant with completely brown/dead wilted leaves standing in a field of healthy green plants. Charcoal Stalk Rot shows stalk cross-sections, Fusarium and Gibberella show ear rot, Diplodia shows stalk breakage, and others don't match the whole-plant wilt pattern.
